sections.title: ① Concept Explanation
sections.body: **ReAct** (Reasoning + Acting) is a prompting paradigm introduced in the 2022 paper "ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models." It interleaves **Thought** (the LLM's internal reasoning), **Action** (a tool call), and **Observation** (the tool result) in a structured loop. Unlike pure chain-of-thought (reasoning only) or pure acting (tools without reasoning), ReAct combines both — the LLM reasons about what to do, acts, observes the result, and reasons again. This pattern dramatically improves tool-use accuracy because the LLM can self-correct mid-task based on actual observations. In production, virtually all modern agent frameworks (LangChain AgentExecutor, OpenAI Assistants, LangGraph) implement a variant of ReAct.

diagrams.title: ReAct: Thought → Action → Observation, repeated
diagrams.mermaid:
sequenceDiagram
  participant U as User
  participant LLM as LLM
  participant T as Tool
  U->>LLM: What is the weather in Paris in Fahrenheit?
  Note over LLM: Thought - I need the current weather
  LLM->>T: Action get_weather(city=Paris)
  T-->>LLM: Observation 18 C, cloudy
  Note over LLM: Thought - convert 18 C to F
  LLM->>T: Action calculator(18*9/5+32)
  T-->>LLM: Observation 64.4
  Note over LLM: Thought - I can answer now
  LLM-->>U: Final answer - 64.4 F and cloudy
diagrams.explain: ReAct interleaves **reasoning** (Thought) with **acting** (Action) and feeds each tool result back as an **Observation**. Every observation is appended to the prompt, so the next thought is grounded in real data instead of guesses. The loop ends when the model emits a final answer — or when your **max-iterations** guard stops it.

sections.title: ④ Visual Explanation
sections.body:
```
REACT (REASONING + ACTING) PATTERN
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

ORIGINAL CHAIN-OF-THOUGHT (No grounding):
──────────────────────────────────────────
User: "What is AAPL's P/E ratio?"
LLM Thought 1: "AAPL is a technology company..."
LLM Thought 2: "Its P/E is around 25..."  ← HALLUCINATION (no real data)
LLM Answer: "28" ← May be wrong!

REACT (Grounded reasoning):
────────────────────────────
User: "What is AAPL's P/E ratio?"
                │
                ▼
┌──────────────────────────────────────┐
│ THOUGHT: I need to look up AAPL's    │
│ current P/E ratio using a tool.      │
└──────────────────┬───────────────────┘
                   │
                   ▼
┌──────────────────────────────────────┐
│ ACTION: get_financial_data(          │
│   ticker="AAPL", metric="pe_ratio"  │
│ )                                    │
└──────────────────┬───────────────────┘
                   │
                   ▼
┌──────────────────────────────────────┐
│ OBSERVATION: {"pe_ratio": 28.4,      │
│  "as_of": "2026-05-25"}             │
└──────────────────┬───────────────────┘
                   │
                   ▼
┌──────────────────────────────────────┐
│ THOUGHT: I have the real data.       │
│ P/E is 28.4 as of today.            │
│ I can now answer definitively.       │
└──────────────────┬───────────────────┘
                   │
                   ▼
           FINAL ANSWER: "AAPL P/E = 28.4 (as of 2026-05-25)"
                         ← GROUNDED, ACCURATE

REACT vs ALTERNATIVES:
═══════════════════════
         CoT           ReAct          ReAct + Reflexion
        ─────          ─────          ─────────────────
Think ──► Answer   Think ──► Act    Think ──► Act
                      │        │       │        │
                   Observe ◄──┘    Observe ◄──┘
                      │                │
                   Think              Think
                      │                │
                   Answer            Reflect ──► Memory
                                       │
                                    Next Run
                                   (improved)
```

quiz.question: What are the limitations of the original ReAct paper's approach?
options: The system prompt is the agent's constitution — it defines identity, capabilities, constraints, output format, and behavioral guardrails.

Autonomy — Agents act without per-step human instruction; chatbots respond to every message; Tool Use — Agents call external APIs and tools; chatbots only generate text; Goal Persistence — Agents maintain a goal across multiple steps; chatbots answer one message at a time.
deterministic agent** follows fixed control flow — the same input always produces the same sequence of actions (e.g., rule-based workflow).

No parallel actions — ReAct is strictly sequential (think → act → observe → think...); Verbose token usage — Repeating Thought/Action/Observation format consumes many tokens; Hallucinated observations — Without stop tokens, the LLM may fabricate observations.
quiz.explanation: No parallel actions — ReAct is strictly sequential (think → act → observe → think...) Verbose token usage — Repeating Thought/Action/Observation format consumes many tokens Hallucinated observations — Without stop tokens, the LLM may fabricate observations No structured tool schemas — Original used free-text tool descriptions, leading to format errors Single-agent — No notion of delegation or subagents Modern…

quiz.question: How does OpenAI's function calling implement ReAct under the hood?
options: State is the live, mutable snapshot of the agent's current execution context — what step it's on, what variables are set, what tools have been called.

Use a risk-autonomy matrix: Low risk + high predictability → Full autonomy (no human in loop); High risk + high predictability → Human approval for specific action types; Low risk + low predictability → Agent acts, human reviews async.

Follow this 6-step design process: Define the goal space — What tasks will this agent solve? What's out of scope?; Identify required tools — What external capabilities are needed (search, DB, APIs)?; Design the memory architecture — Short-term (context window), long-term (vector store)?.

OpenAI's function calling is a structured version of ReAct where: Thought = The LLM's internal reasoning (hidden, not shown in message); Action = tool_calls field in the response (structured JSON, not free-text); Observation = The role: "tool" message added to conversation.
quiz.explanation: OpenAI's function calling is a structured version of ReAct where: Thought = The LLM's internal reasoning (hidden, not shown in message) Action = tool_calls field in the response (structured JSON, not free-text) Observation = The role: "tool" message added to conversation The key improvement over original ReAct: tool arguments are validated JSON (no parsing errors), and the model is trained to output structured…

quiz.explanation: Reflexion adds a fourth step: Reflect — after completing a task, the agent reviews whether its answer was correct, identifies mistakes, and stores lessons in memory for the next attempt. ReAct is reactive (respond to observations); Reflexion is self-improving (learns from outcomes).

quiz.question: What is the role of the "scratchpad" in ReAct implementations?
options: deterministic agent** follows fixed control flow — the same input always produces the same sequence of actions (e.g., rule-based workflow).
The system prompt is the agent's constitution — it defines identity, capabilities, constraints, output format, and behavioral guardrails.

Autonomy — Agents act without per-step human instruction; chatbots respond to every message; Tool Use — Agents call external APIs and tools; chatbots only generate text; Goal Persistence — Agents maintain a goal across multiple steps; chatbots answer one message at a time.
The scratchpad is the accumulated Thought+Action+Observation history within a single agent run.
quiz.explanation: The scratchpad is the accumulated Thought+Action+Observation history within a single agent run. It's the agent's working memory for the current task. In practice, it's implemented as additional messages appended to the conversation context.

quiz.question: How do you evaluate the quality of a ReAct agent's reasoning vs. its action selection?
options: (Q2-Q10 cover: hierarchical planning, goal setting formats (SMART goals), dependency graphs, replanning triggers, parallel step execution, plan validation before…

The context window is the agent's working memory limit. Every message (system prompt + conversation + tool results) consumes tokens. When the context fills up, the agent loses earlier information — causing goal drift, repeated actions, and hallucination. Mitigation strategies: Sliding window: Keep only last N messages; Summarization: Compress old turns into a summary message; Selective memory: Score messages by relevance and prune low-score ones.

Termination conditions prevent infinite loops: Max iterations — Hard cap on loop count; Confidence threshold — Agent signals sufficient confidence in answer; Goal achievement signal — LLM explicitly outputs FINAL_ANSWER.

Separate evaluation: Reasoning quality: Does the Thought correctly identify what's needed? (Human review or LLM-as-judge); Action selection: Does the agent pick the right tool and arguments? (Compare against golden dataset); Observation utilization: Does the agent correctly use the observation to update its next thought?.
